scale.notes: 1 block = 2 m vertical, 1 block = 4 m horizontal. Signature details (blast doors, springs, Battle Cab displays) scaled up 2x in local context for visibility. Locked by deliberation Topic 1.

recommended_mod: CubicWorld or similar with at least 2,048 block build height

world_origin.description: Sea level, centered on the mountain's vertical axis. Vanilla sea level convention.

mountain.geology: Pink-to-brick-red Pikes Peak granite (syenogranite). Minecraft: pink terracotta, red granite, polished andesite.

public_entrance_gate.description: At the base of the mountain, north side, where the approach road begins.

parking_lot.description: 40 x 70 block gravel area, switchback terminus, halfway up the mountain.

security_checkpoint_trailer.description: Small oak building at the parking lot gate.

north_portal.description: Small concrete-and-steel arch on the north face of the central peak, ~70% up the mountain. Faces north. The build origin for the below-ground layout.

approach_road_final_switchback.description: Final switchback from parking lot to portal arch. Climbs 500 blocks of elevation. Surface: smooth stone or light grey concrete.

approach_road_main.description: Main approach road from public gate to parking lot. Switchback through forest. Surface: coarse dirt, gravel, podzol.

support_buildings.description: Backup power building on a shelf below the central peak.
Water pump building lower on the east side.

portal_entrance_interior.description: Build origin. Where the visitor steps into the tunnel.

tunnel_leg_1_end.description: End of Leg 1 (south, descending) of the J-curve tunnel. ~200 blocks from portal.

blast_door_side_branch.description: Side-branch off Leg 1, ~250 blocks into tunnel. Houses both 25-ton blast doors and the airlock chamber. Cinematic reveal of the build.

tunnel_bend_1.description: First J-curve bend, where the tunnel turns from south to east.

tunnel_leg_2_end.description: End of Leg 2 (east) of the tunnel. ~500 blocks from portal.

tunnel_bend_2.description: Second J-curve bend, where the tunnel turns from east to south.

chamber_entry.description: Where the tunnel opens into the main chamber. ~800 blocks from portal.

main_chamber_center.description: Center of the main chamber complex. The 15 buildings are arranged in a 5x3 grid around this point.

main_chamber_bounds.description: The 45 wide x 18 tall x 25 deep block chamber volume.

reservoir.description: Underground lake, offset to the west of the main chamber. 30 x 15 x 20 blocks. Connected to the chamber by a 30-block access tunnel.

battle_cab.description: The Command Center. Centerpiece of the build, in the central building of the 5x3 grid. The climax of the visitor experience.

power_plant_room.description: 6 diesel generators + battery bank. Off the south side of the chamber.

diesel_reservoir_room.description: Sealed diesel storage, black concrete, magma block floor.

air_intake_blast_valve.description: Single visible blast valve on the south chamber wall. Faded reference, not a tourable room.

emergency_egress_door.description: Single locked iron door at the far end of the reservoir. Signed 'EMERGENCY EGRESS.' Faded reference only.

legs.description: South, descending gradually. The visitor cannot see the far end.
Smooth 90 degree curve, south to east.
East, mostly level with slight ascent to chamber elevation.
Smooth 90 degree curve, east to south.
South, level. The chamber becomes visible at the end. Total length across all legs and bends is ~860; the deliberation's ~800 is approximate.

tunnel_path.surface: Light grey concrete, with rough pink-and-grey granite walls and iron-bar rock bolts in the ceiling.

blast_door_assembly.configuration: Two 25-ton blast doors in sequence with an airlock chamber between. Both doors open (post-1992 status). Doors are 5x4 iron-block, hinged outward, scaled 2x in local context. Single backlight from the airlock.

buildings.name: Air Defense Operations Center
buildings.interior_theme: Radar-tracking screens, multiple smaller displays in a grid with circular radar sweeps

buildings.name: Missile Warning Center
buildings.interior_theme: Data-room, wall of status screens in a 4x3 grid, optional 1979 false alarm plaque

buildings.name: Space Control Center
buildings.interior_theme: Orbital tracking, star map on ceiling, globe projection on main display

buildings.name: Combined Intelligence Watch
buildings.interior_theme: Smaller briefing-style room, one large screen, a table, fewer consoles, Chrystal Palace code-name sign

buildings.name: Battle Cab (Command Center)
buildings.interior_theme: Centerpiece. U-shaped tiered consoles, wall of displays with world map, time-zone clocks (ZULU / EXERCISE / HAWAII / PACIFIC / MOUNTAIN / CENTRAL / EASTERN / MOSCOW), 'WELCOME TO THE NORAD COMMAND CENTER' ticker, 1980 false alarm plaque on back wall. The climax of the build.

buildings.name: Chapel
buildings.interior_theme: Pews (oak stairs), altar (oak slab), single candle (lantern), dim warm lighting. The only quiet room in the build.

buildings.name: Granite Inn (bar)
buildings.interior_theme: Bar counter (oak slabs), stools (oak stairs), bottles (potions/honey bottles), 'GRANITE INN' sign, warm amber lighting (shroomlights, candles). The only warm light in the build.

buildings.name: (Support / medical-dental)
buildings.notes: Optional subtle ambient sway animation (0.25 block, redstone clock + piston). Single nod, not a full build.

buildings.name: (Stargate Command corridor)
buildings.interior_theme: Back-corridor room with a single door signed 'STARGATE COMMAND.' Nothing else. The in-joke from the real broom closet.

building_composition.source: Locked by deliberation Topic 3 (Air & Space Forces Magazine, Air Force magazine of record)

chamber_array.form: Single rectangular chamber with 15 free-standing buildings arranged in a 5x3 grid. Real complex has 3 parallel main tunnels intersected by 4 cross tunnels; in compressed scale this is rendered as one larger unified chamber.
chamber_array.ceiling: Bare pink granite with rock bolts. One small concrete-dome repair (6x6 blocks) referencing the 1962 fault-repair dome.
chamber_array.floor: Light grey concrete (smooth stone slab variant) with industrial metal grating in service areas.
signage: 1,319 SPRINGS - 1,000 LB EACH - INSTALLED 1964 - NEVER REPLACED
NORMAL SHOCK: 1 INCH BUILDING MOVEMENT. EXTREME EVENT: 12 INCHES.
APRIL 20, 1966 - COMBAT OPERATIONS CENTER DECLARED OPERATIONAL (SECONDARY)
OPERATIONS CENTER INTERIORS ARE DESIGNER INTERPRETATIONS BASED ON DECLASSIFIED PUBLIC INFORMATION, 2006-2016 PUBLIC PHOTOGRAPHS, AND THE 1978 GAO REPORT.

service_tunnel_to_subtropolis.description: Service tunnel from the south end of the Cheyenne chamber, descending through the south wall of the mountain, crossing the ravine at y~150-200, and continuing south to SubTropolis. Flagged for the combined-complex team; not budgeted in this build.

public_shaft_to_city.description: Public shaft / funicular from the Cheyenne exit down to the city in the ravine. The visitor's exit in the combined complex instead of walking back through the tunnel. Flagged for the combined-complex team.

ravine_north_wall_cheyenne_side.description: The mountain's south face borders the ravine.

city_center_combined.description: City in the ravine valley, ~500 blocks south of the Cheyenne portal. Defined in the combined-complex report.

subtropolis_center_combined.description: SubTropolis complex on the south side of the ravine, ~800 blocks south of the Cheyenne portal. Defined in the SubTropolis site plan.

exterior_granite.description: Pink-to-brick-red Pikes Peak granite substitute. Dominant exterior material.

scale_verification.recommended_mod: CubicWorld or similar with at least 2,048 block build height
